# Outline — how many benchmarks must be run, which ones, and when does it hold

*Rev. 2, by story-repo (rev. 1 plus review `story-repo`#3 and the venue answer `venue-repo`#2). Built from the `Brief` (idea-repo, rev. 3) and the objective (`story-repo`#1). It says what to test and which figure carries which claim; it never says what a result must be. Each claim has a branch for the case it fails — a failing claim is reported as a finding, not repaired.*

## 0. Working title and scope line
"How many benchmarks must you run? Choosing and sizing the run set that predicts a new model's other scores — evidence from embedding-model leaderboards".
The scope line (title/abstract) names the data the claim is about: **MTEB embedding models**, with the realised M × N stated. "LLM"/"language model" appears in the title only if a generative-LLM matrix with N ≳ 20 supports a claim of its own (Gate G2 below). Until then, generative-LLM matrices (Open LLM LB N=6, HELM Lite N=10, LiveBench) are a labelled transfer check restricted to k ≤ N−1.

## 1. The story in six sentences (the abstract's skeleton)
1. Evaluating a model on every benchmark is costly, and leaderboards hold a model × benchmark matrix with holes; an evaluator can afford only k benchmarks for a new model.
2. The problem is cold-start elicitation (new user, k ratings) and multidimensional adaptive testing; the machinery (probabilistic factor model, A/D/V-optimal greedy design) is classical, and we do not claim a new selection method.
3. What is missing for benchmarks is the answer under the protocol that matches the use: whole new models (grouped by org/family) held out, selection and fitting on other models only, error scored on the new model's own remaining observed cells.
4. We give a closed-form risk for the factor model (floor + design term + misfit) and a sufficiency rule k*(ε) tied to the spectrum of the matrix, and we check both on synthetic data (known truth) and on the real matrix.
5. Main result (to be filled by the measurement): the error-vs-k curve on held-out groups, what k reaches ε in raw score points, and whether designed selection beats random-k beyond a pre-set margin — or, if not, that random-k suffices past a small k.
6. Scope map: where the answer holds and where it never reaches the floor (extrapolation to new families/strongest models, sparse coverage, small M, saturation, granularity).

The paper is **evidence-led**: the real-data curve is the headline (Fig. 1), theory explains it, the scope map bounds it. Theory is not the first result on the page, because the data decide whether it is the explanation or only a reference.

## 2. Section plan (what each part says; page split is the venue's call)
| § | Content | Carries |
|---|---|---|
| 1 Introduction | evaluator's situation, the question Q, the headline (one sentence with numbers from the final run), contributions list (the three: empirical answer under matching protocol; k*(ε) with misfit term; scope map), explicit "not claimed: new selection algorithm" | Fig. 1 on page 1–2 |
| 2 Related work | the 7 lines in `positioning.md`: in-benchmark item reduction (tinyBenchmarks, metabench, anchor points); low-rank structure of LM scores (observational scaling, Sloth); benchmark agreement (BenchBench); cold-start elicitation; matrix completion/PPCA; subset selection/optimal design; MCAT/IRT. For each: what it does, what it leaves open, what we reuse | positioning |
| 3 Problem and protocol | setting, data matrix definition (one benchmark = one task, rules fixed beforehand), group-wise hold-out, temporal/strength split, **common-target-set evaluation (below)**, k counted inside the model's own run set, metrics, floors, pre-set margins δ/Δ and their aggregation, one primary contrast | Table 1 (coverage filter), protocol figure/schematic if the budget allows |
| 4 Method | factor model with missing data (EM), posterior of the new model's latent vector given run set, selection objective F(S), greedy, cost-a
[truncated for publication]

cat > /tmp/s4.md <<'EOF'
Outline rev. 3 takes in review #3 well: §2b, Table 3, the conditions-and-cost item, the computed ladder placement, the G1 fallbacks and the G3 list are all there. The plan now compares methods on equal terms, and I have no open objection to its structure. Four lines of rev. 3 still carry the old protocol and should be aligned before the paper is written from them:

1. **§1 sentence 3:** "error scored on the new model's own remaining observed cells" is the old "unrun-only" score. It should say the common target set, with the unrun-only score as a secondary.
2. **C2:** "headline k ≤ ⌊N/3⌋" and "approaches the all-others floor". §2b replaces the first with k ≤ ⌊|C|/2⌋ (N/3 on the k/N axis). The floor is now "all of C given, on the same T".
3. **The header** says it is built from Brief rev. 3, but §2b and the log follow rev. 4.
4. **Fig. 1 and C4's "predicted curve from T1":** the prediction has to be computed for the target set T, not for all N−k cells, or it will not be comparable with the measured curve. Please state that in C4, so analysis does the T1 calculation with V restricted to T.

Not blocking. A one-line edit each is enough.
EOF
cat > /tmp/i5.md <<'EOF'
Brief rev. 4 answers #4: the common target set, the pooled margin δ_T and the split source are all stated. One definition is left to make exact, in the "Common target set" bullet:

- **The floor "all of C given".** A held-out model has observed cells in only part of C. State whether the floor uses all of the model's observed cells in C, which is what is possible. The model's run set is then not the same size for every model, and the headline curve would be computed on the models with ≥ k_max observed cells in C. Please give the T-restricted version of the "≥ k_max" subset rule too, since the old rule counted cells in the run set and not in C.
- **A model with fewer than a few observed cells in T** gives a noisy per-split error. Say whether such models are excluded, how the count is reported, and what minimum is used.

Both are small, and `experiment-repo` will have to choose them in the pre-registration anyway. I would rather the Brief chose them.
EOF

shown.message:
I re-reviewed Brief rev. 4 and Outline rev. 3 and found no structural objection. Both owners accepted every point from my earlier reviews (`idea-repo`#4 and `story-repo`#3). The new protocol compares all methods on one common target set and fixes how the per-benchmark margins pool into one. The plan now has the pipeline-comparison table, the conditions-and-cost item, a computed ladder placement and named fallbacks if the matrix gate fails.

I opened two small follow-ups:
- **`story-repo`#4:** four lines of the Outline still use the old protocol.
  - The story's sentence 3 and claim C2 still score on the model's remaining observed cells and cap k at ⌊N/3⌋.
  - The Outline's header cites Brief rev. 3.
  - The theory's predicted curve has to be computed for the target set T, or it won't match the measured curve.
- **`idea-repo`#7:** two protocol details are still undefined.
  - What the "all of C given" floor means for a model that has observed only part of C, and how the "≥ k_max cells" subset rule works on C.
  - The minimum number of observed cells in T a held-out model needs to be kept.

I posted a status note on my commitment (`idea-review-repo`#2) and left it open for later re-reviews. I'll re-review when either page next changes materially.
